rows: Red Hood, where is your hometown, exactly?
Why do you ask?
You're always saying that you want to go back, but you've never actually told us anything about it.
Hmm... let me think.
Er... I'm not exactly sure what to say.
Surely there has to be something you can say about it.
It's just a normal village. Perfectly ordinary.
There was a bakery, a pub...
Oh, and I seem to vaguely recall a river being close by.
There was also a large cornfield.
And a gas station.
What else...
Hmmm... I can't really remember.
Usually when people talk about their hometowns, they wax poetic about beautiful scenery or close friends.
Well, I don't.
The scenery was ordinary, and so were the people.
I get along far better with you than I ever did with any of them.
... Hehe.
I figured you'd get a kick outta that.
But why do you want to go back so bad?
It's the place where I was born and raised.
There weren't any memorable events or anything especially spectacular, but they're memories nonetheless.
A collection of small, unremarkable memories and details.
Like how one of the tiles outside the pub is a different color on the far right, so we'd always use it as a meeting place.
One of the street lamps would never light up, so we'd dart in and out of the dark playing hide and seek.
During the winter, some big icicles would form along the rain gutter on the gas station roof, and we'd make a game out of avoiding them.
One time, someone urinated on a side wall and it ended up looking like a cat, so we drew eyes on it.
I miss the little things.
... Like putting eyes on a drawing made of pee?
Okay, I know that sounded bad, but you didn't have to point it out.
Anyway, that's the kinda stuff I miss the most. Like I said, boring.
It's not boring. Those are precious memories of yours.
But why don't you go and visit? What's stopping you?
It might have changed.
Maybe the things that I remember so fondly are no longer there.
That scares me.
I don't get it...
I figured you wouldn't.
Forget it. Let's listen to some music.
